newsitem.title: FRANCE: French Socialists back EMU with conditions.
newsitem.headline: French Socialists back EMU with conditions.

text.p: France's opposition Socialist party said on Friday it backed the launch of a single European currency but said it wanted all European Union members to join if they wanted to do so.

"Membership by Italy and Spain seems to us necessary and possible, as well as by Britain, if it wants it," it said in the party's official manifesto for a two-round parliamentary election on May 25 and June 1.
It said Europe, when deciding which countries qualify to join monetary union, must take account of the trend shown towards meeting Maastricht Treaty criteria, as allowed for in the treaty itself.

It called for a social and political dimension in Europe, by substituting a "solidarity and growth pact" for an "austerity pact" -- an apparent reference to the stability pact agreed by EU leaders last year to limit budget deficits.
There must be a European economic government alongside the future European Central Bank, and the new euro must not be overvalued against the dollar and the yen, it said.
It noted the euro was due to be launched on January 1, 1999, and said its response was "to say yes to the switch to the euro, but under certain conditions".
